chapter_theme: Songs at Srimushnam (ஸ்ரீமுஷ்டம், திருமுட்டம்): one asks Murugan to appear wearing every kind of pearl garland on the peacock with his consort and devotees; the other rejects courtesans who snatch money and ruin families; the praise names the goddess, Devayanai, and the daughter of Adi Varaha.
structure_note: 760 is a vision prayer with no confession; 761 is a courtesan song.

760.reading: The poet asks Murugan to come before him on the green peacock with his consort and the throng of his servants, wearing on his chest garlands of pearls from bamboo, cloud, elephant, mountain, conch, sea, serpent and fire. The praise names the mother who bore us, bright as rain-cloud and lisping like cuckoo and parrot, the dark-throated Siva with datura, Murugan their son, the bridegroom of Devayanai and of the lady of release, who cut the bonds of the gods Sura had imprisoned, at Thirumuttam.
760.nuance: The pearl list follows the traditional sources of pearls (bamboo, cloud, elephant tusk, conch, sea, cobra), each as a separate garland; the plea is simply to see. அடிமைக் குழாமொடு: Murugan is asked to come with the company of his servants, not alone. திருமுத்தி மாதின் மணவாளா, bridegroom of the lady of release, is either a name of Valli or a figure.

761.reading: The poet describes women with arrow-eyes and bow brows who stir deep infatuation and dance to the beat, and calls them greedy prostitutes who snatch money, deceivers, sinners, worn by excess, quarrel-makers, ruiners of families, and asks whether their friendship befits him. The praise names Siva who burned Kama with laughter, the goddess at his side who bore the three worlds, Rama who churned the sea with Vasuki and gave the first nectar, and Murugan who sported with the daughter of Adi Varaha at Thirumuttam.
761.nuance: The second half of the confession is a run of abusive nouns in -கள் (பறிகாரிகள், மாறிகள், கேடிகள்) set to the rhythm; பணம் எத்தப் பறிகாரிகள் and குடிகேடிகள் carry the charge. ஆதிவராகர் தம் மகள் makes Valli the daughter of Vishnu as the Boar, whose temple is at Srimushnam.

links.note: The Kural names double-minded women with liquor and gambling as the company of those whom fortune has left; 761 calls the women குடிகேடிகள், ruiners of families.
